title: Asbestos Survey Before Remodeling Everett WA — Clean Air Agency Rules, Testing, Abatement and Permits
description: An Everett homeowner's guide to asbestos before a remodel: when a survey is required, who can do it, which materials in older homes get tested, Washington L&I abatement rules, Clean Air Agency notification, disposal, and how it fits with Everett permits.
outline: Why asbestos comes up in Everett remodels
Two sets of rules: the air agency and L&I
Who has to do the survey
Materials that commonly get tested in older Everett homes
Cement-asbestos siding: a common Everett case
How the survey fits with Everett permits
How to shortlist and verify the crew
Next steps for an Everett remodel
search_intent: An Everett homeowner planning a remodel wants to know whether an asbestos survey is required, who may do it, which materials get tested, what the Clean Air Agency and L&I require for removal and notification, where asbestos waste goes, and how it fits with Everett permits.
local_angles: Clean Air Agency Homeowner Renovation: owner-occupied single-family remodel may self-survey; rentals, condos and demolition need an AHERA-certified inspector
L&I: good faith inspection before remodel regardless of building age; owners and contractors subject to mandatory daily fine; certified abatement contractor list
RCW 49.26.013: owner must give written survey report to contractors before they bid
Agency notification: Single-Family Residence Notification with filing fee; none for <10 lf / 48 sf friable per year or nonfriable; demolition needs notification and 10-day wait
No landfills or transfer stations in Snohomish County authorized to receive asbestos waste
Everett Permit Services at 2930 Wetmore Ave, 425-257-8810; online permitting portal; demolition checklist requires agency notification before asbestos removal or demolition
